subject: Brief latency surge on hosted API — customer advisory and follow-up
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme.ai, Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Brief latency surge on hosted API — customer advisory and follow-up

Hi Samir / Acme ops team —

We observed a short-lived latency surge affecting hosted-generation endpoints (primarily POST /v1/generate) between 08:44 and 09:02 PT this morning. Impact summary: p95 latency rose from ~220ms to ~1.2s and a small fraction (~0.8%) of requests returned 502s during the window. We mitigated by routing affected traffic to warmed fallback pools and temporarily increasing routing headroom; normal p95 resumed by 09:06 PT.

Immediate actions we took:
- Identified a small subset of hosts showing kernel-level CPU contention and increased GC on the inference runtime.
- Activated fallback routing to compatible model variants for affected customer requests.
- Cleared a transient batching backlog for impacted queues.

Attachments: inc-snapshot-20261123.png (early telemetry), prelim-timeline-1123.pdf (short timeline). We'll post a short notice on status.redwood.com and follow up with a more detailed timeline once the investigation completes.

Ask: Can you confirm whether your team saw any customer-facing errors or timeouts that we should correlate? We'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up call if helpful.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority. I'll loop in the on-call infra and runtime leads for root cause.

Thanks,
Mina
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Brief latency surge on hosted API — customer advisory and follow-up

Thanks Mina — quick Q: do we have a sense if the contention was caused by a kernel upgrade or a workload change (larger sequences, more concurrent small requests)? If it's the latter, we should check recent rollout metrics for the batching delta. Happy to join the call.

-Ben

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brief latency surge on hosted API — customer advisory and follow-up

Hi Samir — thanks for the quick confirmation and for gathering request IDs. Short answers:
- We do not anticipate token-accounting discrepancies; the surge produced higher latency and a small number of 502s but billing events should align with observed requests. We'll validate counters and confirm in the post-incident summary.
- Preliminary root cause: localized CPU scheduling pressure on three hosts in the us-west-2 pool, amplified by an unexpected burst of concurrent short-sequence requests that increased kernel preemption latency for the runtime thread. No kernel upgrade coincident with the window — investigation points toward a workload burst and an inefficient path in the runtime's batching slot reclaim logic.

Next steps (we own these and will update you):
1) Collect full heap and runtime traces from the three affected hosts (in progress).
2) Validate token accounting and billing counters against request logs you provide.
3) Produce a customer-facing post-incident note and a technical postmortem with timeline and mitigation steps (target by 2026-11-25 EOD).
4) Short-term mitigation: routing policy change to increase headroom for small-request bursts and a patch to the batching reclaim path (can be staged within 48 hours).

I'll post the status page entry now (link included) and share the investigation doc: https://drive.redwood.com/incident/ACME-1123-investigation (read/write for ops@acme.ai). If you prefer a call, we can do a 30-min sync at 11:00 PT — I'll schedule if you confirm.

Appreciate the logs; they'll help validate counters.

Mina
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: ACME latency spike — postmortem actions and customer comms

Team — quick internal summary and owner list following our investigation progress:

Summary: small window of elevated p95 and ~0.8% 502s (08:44–09:02 PT 11/23). Root cause (prelim): CPU scheduling pressure on 3 hosts + batching reclaim inefficiency triggered by concurrent small-sequence bursts. No user data exposure and no billing discrepancies identified in initial checks.

Owners / next steps:
- Marcus Lin: finalize host-level traces and attach full diagnostic bundle to the investigation doc (target 2026-11-24 18:00 PT).
- Jordan Blake: verify routing policy changes were persisted and provide rollback plan (target 2026-11-25 12:00 PT).
- Ben Carter: own the patch for batching reclaim path and plan staging cadence (target PR by 2026-11-26).
- Mina Haddad: customer-facing post-incident summary draft (target 2026-11-25 EOD) and status page closure note.

Customer communication guidance: keep the public status page terse and link to the scheduled postmortem doc for technical readers. Emphasize that normal service resumed automatically and that we have both short-term mitigations and a targeted fix.

I'll circulate the draft for review before publish. CC'd: leadership if we need to escalate wording.

Thanks,
Mina
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
